scope.reviewed: body/literal ownership, peak scan, mode/count/scale arithmetic, division calls and output effects on the tested configurations

findings.result: Independent extraction confirms code [0x48CC,0x49CE) is 258 bytes and referenced literal [0x49D0,0x49D4) is little-endian 0x0000FFFF. The adjacent instruction at 0x49CE is outside the owned code range.

The disassembly agrees with the pseudocode: effective count is at least 3; mode low bits gate the scan; a first maximum item is selected only when center plus available neighbors strictly improves the prior sum; spacing bit 8 changes the divisor and center offset; right-minus-left is multiplied with 32-bit wrap and passed to the original signed divider; final value is rounded by +127 then shifted and stored, with scratch count set. R4-R11 and SP are restored; R0 is not treated as a status contract.

An isolated rerun passed all 600 cases and produced replay JSON byte-identical to the frozen candidate. Candidate receipt-listed files and source image hash verified. Fixtures include the stated count/mode/span/value pattern combinations and check output count/value, trailing destination sentinels, saved registers and SP.

limitations: Fixtures use separate mapped buffers and bounded input layouts; aliasing, concurrency, caller reachability, and item allocation guarantees are unresolved.
Only the tested mode, count, span, and value families are covered; this is not all-input proof.
No physical sensor meaning, canonical admission, or C implementation is claimed.
